mappings.note: Picks the profitable business out of langar, Van Mahotsav and neighbourhood cleaning - the economic/non-economic classification, so CG-SST4.
Defines the market as the place where goods and services are exchanged; CG-SST4 names the market among the institutions pupils should understand.
A Sunday park clean-up enhancing community well-being - unpaid work with social value, so CG-SST4.
Rules out acts done purely for love from the marks of economic activity; the classification again, hence CG-SST4.
Festivals valued for the bonds and identity they build though no money changes hands - the worth of non-economic work, so CG-SST4.
Sorts a pilot's job, a student's homework and blood donation into economic and non-economic; the classification demand, so CG-SST4.
An artisan turning 50 rupees of clay into a 500-rupee vase: value addition (CG-SST4) through a named craft occupation (LO-297).
Statement set checking whether the pilot's job, family cooking and free computer teaching are correctly classified - CG-SST4.
Names value addition from the carpenter's transformation of wood into furniture: the market concept (CG-SST4) in a named trade (LO-297).
The langar as non-economic BECAUSE it is driven by seva: a traditional value (LO-300) explaining unpaid service (CG-SST4).
Swachh Bharat and Van Mahotsav depending on collective participation - the contribution of ordinary citizens, so CG-SST4.
Kavya's uncle operating a bulldozer for a construction company; a named occupation and the sector that offers it, so LO-297.
Payment in kind as compensation in goods rather than cash - a form of payment in the market, so CG-SST4.
Profit against service as the motive separating economic from non-economic work; the chapter's central distinction, hence CG-SST4.
A damaged duplicate whose supplied answer is that cleanliness drives depend on both individual responsibility and collective effort; either way the content is unpaid civic work, so CG-SST4.
Rejects a high-charging doctor as an example of seva among langar, prasad and Swachh Bharat volunteering: the meaning of seva (LO-300) against paid work (CG-SST4).
Statement set on salary, wage and fee, rejecting the claim that a fee is for volunteer service - forms of compensation, so CG-SST4.
Economic activity transforming inputs into a more valuable form, per the carpenter example; the value-addition concept, so CG-SST4.
Recalls Geeta Aunty's profession as an Air Force pilot - a named occupation, so LO-297.
Kabir's grandfather retired from the Border Security Force; his former paid occupation, so LO-297. His unpaid activities are mapped to CG-SST4.
The grandfather's free Geography classes - unpaid contribution to the neighbourhood, hence CG-SST4.
Balancing paid and voluntary work for a well-rounded life and a healthy society - the chapter's evaluative thesis, so CG-SST4.

Asks what the absence of a word for 'cousin' says about Indian family structure. This is Family and Community material sitting in a chapter on work; CG-SST4 does name the family among the institutions, so the item is mapped on its own content.
The grandfather's post-retirement teaching and gardening showing that work has worth beyond pay - the chapter's central claim, so CG-SST4.
Analyses value addition through the carpenter's 600-to-1,000 rupee transformation: the market concept (CG-SST4) in a named trade (LO-297).

Compares salary, fee and daily wage part-paid in kind across a bulldozer operator, a post office employee and a farm labourer: forms of payment (CG-SST4) across named rural and urban occupations (LO-297).
The value generated by seva in langars and by Swachh Bharat: a traditional value (LO-300) producing unpaid social benefit (CG-SST4).
Van Mahotsav plantation drives serving both the environment and social cohesion - collective unpaid work, so CG-SST4.
Defines economic activity as exchange for money or money's worth; the short-answer form of the core definition.
What motivates unpaid work - gratitude, love, care - with family cooking as the example; the non-economic half of the classification, so CG-SST4.
Why the grandfather's free teaching counts as non-economic: no payment passes. The classification applied to one case, hence CG-SST4.
The Kamlapur highway cutting a five-hour trip to two: public infrastructure (LO-294) delivering economic benefit to villagers (CG-SST4).
Kavya's uncle's work as a construction technician and his monthly salary: the occupation (LO-297) and its form of pay (CG-SST4).
Caring for a sick grandparent as non-economic because it is done from love and duty - the classification, so CG-SST4.
The purpose of Van Mahotsav, namely awareness and plantation drives; collective unpaid work, mapped with the other campaign items.
Why selling school bags is economic - goods exchanged for money: the classification (CG-SST4) applied to a trading occupation (LO-297).
Parents helping with schoolwork as non-economic, done from love; the classification again, so CG-SST4.
A truck driver's transport service earning payment and easing trade: a named occupation (LO-297) contributing economically (CG-SST4).
A kitchen garden for one's own use against a farmer selling produce: the classification (CG-SST4) turning on whether farming is pursued as an occupation (LO-297).
Vivekananda's 'work as worship' applied to paid and unpaid work alike: a value from an Indian system of thought (LO-300) bearing on the worth of work (CG-SST4).
